data.name: Night Crisis
data.detailed_description:
Q: What are the core features?
A: The game is based upon a multiplayer co-op experience. There will be multiple factions of enemies to take down, which may have units on the ground, in the air and on sea.

*ALL DLC WILL BE FREE , NO MICRO TRANSACTIONS OR LOOTBOXES*



Q: What kind of maps can we expect?
A: Maps will be dynamic . This means that maps will feature events like Destructible environments , weather,scripted. There are 12 maps upon release. The size and ‘openness’ of the maps are depending on scenario. Whether you can engage the enemy in vehicular combat or not, is also dependent on the scenario.

Q: What can the player customize in-game?
A: The player will be able to customize the gear which you use in the field, which includes weapons,gadgets and attachments. The player may also be able to be customize the look of his character and weapons, but nothing which can be perceived as absurd.

Q: What kind of weapons will the game have?
A: There will be a set amount of weapons for each class. Currently the weapons are inspired on their military counterparts.

Q: What type of attachments can you expect?
A: Each weapon will allow you to customize your optics, you can also add other attachments like grips, plus some weapons allow you to change the ammo type of your weapon.

Q: How many classes will the game have?
A: So far, we have four classes. It can become a possibility that each class will have a specific type of weapons and gadgets to use.


Q: What type of enemies will you fight?
A: There will be a mixture of human, humanoid and mechanical infantry; ground, aerial and naval vehicles. Hostiles will have advanced moves to use in battle, we’re trying to make them as unpredictable as possible.

Q: What type of game-modes can we expect?
A: So far, we’ve got three
- Annihilation(Survival) (neutralize all hostiles in the area)
- Assault(Domination) (Take control of the target location, you can use various approaches to achieve this)

- Intelligence run (Acquire valuable data from research stations)


Q: Will there be additional monetization?
A: NO.

Q: Will there be support for other Operating systems?
A: The game will have Mac , PS4 , XBOX will be looked into post release.

Q: Will the game have an anti-cheat system?
A: Yes, we are currently looking into which system will be the most fitting to the game.

STORY BACKGROUND
The year is 2020 , the End Times are here. The Matrix is falling for the Global Elites .The Natural Spirit Himself began to destroy the enemy , deploy Natural Disasters, create Heatwaves, expose corrupt leaders . So the Global Colonizers, in fear, began to create a global military police to get their order reform and oppression.

You are the Native Resistance , you are the first and last line of defense against the force known as the United Alliance(Global Elites).
You are fighting for the land , preserving the resources , and human freedom.

reviews.review:
[h1]Introduction[/h1]
Today’s the infamous 420 annual event and I shall not review a stoner-themed game per se, yet the experience in Night Crisis proved somewhat psychedelic nonetheless. As the Steam debut for AlteredPlanets, this indie dev has faced an uphill battle since it picked the online MP-centric shooter genre for its first project. At least it features an original approach which should help Night Crisis stand out from more generic titles catering to a constantly growing segment of players. It wasn’t a smooth run, yet rocky starts are to be expected in our day and gaming age. 

[h1]Story [/h1]
First of all, what do you do as a developer when you haven’t implemented a storyline in your project? Well “improvisation” might be the keyword since Night Crisis took the sandbox route so to speak and it cuts players loose on all its maps unlocked from the moment you start the game. A barebones tutorial section is included, but combat is the only true way you’ll master the gameplay mechanics anyway. Bots have been fortunately added for both well deserved practice and those times during the day when you’ll find few human opponents in Night Crisis’ lobbies. I really wish I could discuss at least about the various factions even if there isn’t a story or campaign mode. A static screen with the basic info on the opposing forces and context, shall be highly appreciated once it may get added in a future update. Don't skip on this, AlteredPlanets.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1697704363

Usurprisingly, a war ensues between human armed forces and their former robotic allies (I told you we can’t trust those drones). For the sake of brevity and since none of this is properly mentioned in-game yet, imagine the “campaign” in Night Crisis as a Matrix-meets-Terminator type of scenario. Just shoot first and ask no further questions, ok? It’s not like battle royales or other shooter subgenres from time immemorial had logical narrative threads either. These are power fantasies and they should never get mixed up with our already bleak reality which may or may not devolve into an actual fight for survival against the robots we so desperately wish to use as future slave labour. When you sow wind you can only reap the storm. It won’t be a bountiful harvest, of that much you can be certain.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]
Moddb reports that this game has been in development since 2014 and that it’s being powered by the Unity Engine. It doesn’t show its age though and my only complaints regarding Night Crisis’ looks, stem from the imbedded motion blur which REALLY needs an option for turning it off if not tone it down. This is the one setting I disable from all my games as soon as I boot them up for the first time. Blur needs to go since it not only interferes with my screenshots, but it also leads to irregular frame rate on higher resolutions. By contrast, I enjoyed the excessive chromatic aberration which adds a personal touch to this title. It actually made me question the in-game allegiance since a sober human soldier would obviously not have his vision impeded in any capacity. Perhaps it’s all a ploy for fighting the enemy from the inside? BSG-style Cylon infiltrators perhaps, but I’m probably reading too much into this. The visuals are nice, it’s a step in the right direction from regular shooters which focus on different shades of brown.

[h1]Audio[/h1]
Sounds are a faltering chapter, sadly. Repetitive and not rising to the quality of the visuals it tries to complement, I ended up muting them and listening to my own tracks. Communication between myself and several human players was never hindered, even if I did play far more against the AI. The latter follows the principle of “Silence is Golden”, but it’s not like I was expecting voice acting from a title which doesn’t showcase a story to begin with.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1697704529

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Arguably the one crucial section in which titles belonging to our subgenre in review must excel, is none other than the gameplay which must fill the gaps left by the absence of a narrative or potential audiovisual shortcomings. At the time of this writing, Night Crisis is far away from its Steam launch woes that have prevented me from getting the full picture in its case. It was thoroughly unplayable about one month ago until the dev team finally started patching it up on a weekly basis, aided by community feedback. An admirable feat, though not unexpected from any serious creator. Yeah, I know very well that MP-centric Steam games have an incredibly high chance of becoming abandonware, but hopefully Night Crisis won’t fall into this predictable pattern. That being said, it’s in dire need of a community.

The lobbies aren’t really ghost towns but I didn’t find nearly as many players as I would have liked, not that I can really complain about the bots’ quality. A class system has been implemented based on weapon distribution but the most striking feature, is the sheer diversity of vehicles. These range from bikes to trucks, tanks, speedboats and no less than three helicopter models. The control scheme can be a bit clunky at times, but they’re still highly efficient methods of gaining an edge in battle. Being constantly  outnumbered is no longer an issue once you pilot an attack chopper. It levels both the playing field and all resistance. Speaking of the maps, there are 13 of them included so far and they’re just as diversified as you’d expect. Urban settings, jungles, deserts, islands and some of my favorites, maps in the open sea with aircraft carriers acting as defense points or assault platforms.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1697704766

[h1]Verdict[/h1]
I think that Night Crisis needs further incentives. A price drop may help in this regard along with more exposure online. A community will seldom form through word of mouth, but you don’t need a huge marketing budget to arouse sufficient interest. I do admit that I liked reading about promises of free DLC packs along with a firm pledge of no microtransactions or lootboxes. Those two are true banes of the multiplayer medium and they’re unfortunately making their rotten way towards singleplayer experiences as well. MP shooters are ironically, a gamble even when they don’t implement such concepts. Night Crisis still has an ace up its sleeve.

[h1]Strong Points[/h1]
+ Pleasant graphics.
+ Decent AI with bots that offer adequate practice.
+ Gameplay diversity through maps, vehicles and weaponry.

[h1]Weak Points[/h1]
- No Steam Achievements or Trading Cards.
- No campaign/storyline.
- Repetitive sounds.

[b]Rating 70/100[/b]
